heading_en: Mixed Text Composition in Horizontal Writing Mode
heading_ja: 横組の和欧文混植に用いる文字

cases.quote: In horizontal writing mode the basic approach is to use proportional Western fonts (Figure 90).
cases.rationale: §3.2.2's own opening sentence restates a classification content that is already owned at M0: `docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own `[[owned]]` entry for §3.2.6 states that proportional Western text is cl-27, and `A.27/latin-capital-a/proportional-frame`'s own case already reads exactly this input for exactly that reason. This case reads the identical input again under §3.2.2's own address, because coverage in this suite is counted per address, not per sentence a case's rationale happens to cite — the precedent `3.1.9/full-stop-at-line-end/table-4-alone-stays-rigid-among-the-three`'s own entry states against §D.1 for a boundary case, and `A.27/european-numeral/proportional-frame`'s own case already quotes this exact §3.2.2 sentence in its own `quote` field while crediting only §3.2.4, §3.2.6, §3.9.1 and §3.9.2 in its `rules` — so the sentence has been read before in this suite and never yet credited to its own home address. Every one of the fifty-two Latin letters is named by three Appendix A tables at once — §A.19 unqualified, §A.25 as 'proportionally-spaced', §A.27 as 'proportionally-spaced' — and the axis that separates §A.19 from the other two is the declared frame: a proportional advance is not the half-width §3.1.2 states for none of these three classes, so §A.19's own listing survives no filtering by width at all and what remains is the tie between §A.25 and §A.27, whose Remarks cells are identical character for character. §3.9.2 defines cl-25 by the construct a Latin or Greek letter sits in, an SI unit symbol, which this occurrence's caller declares nothing of, so §A.25's listing describes nothing here (`docs/adr/0015`); what is left is §A.27, and §3.2.2's own sentence is independently why a caller who followed this document's own basic approach would have declared the proportional frame in the first place, rather than an arbitrary choice this occurrence happens to make. `A.27/latin-capital-a/proportional-frame`'s own input is reused unchanged below, because the point of this case is which address is credited, not a new fact about the letter.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.27's row for U+0041, with §3.2.6's Note and §3.2.2's own basic-approach sentence (§3.9.1, §3.9.2)

forbidden.why: §A.25 lists 0041 with the same Remarks cell as §A.27, so the frame does not separate them and nothing in the tables does. §3.9.2 separates them: cl-25 is the class of characters inside a unit symbol, a fact about the construct this occurrence declares none of. Answering cl-25 from the Remarks column alone makes every proportionally set Latin letter in a horizontal Japanese document a unit symbol.

The answer of an implementation that classifies by the surrounding script rather than by the declared frame. §3.2.2's own basic approach is proportional Western fonts, not the ideographic frame, and §3.2.6's Note assigns the proportional occurrence to cl-27 in so many words.

cases.quote: For European numerals, both half-width fonts and proportional fonts are used.
cases.rationale: §3.2.2's own second sentence states, for horizontal writing mode, the same choice §3.2.6's Note decides a class from: a European numeral may be set on a half-width font or on a proportional one, and this case reads the half-width reading, already owned at M0. `docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own `[[owned]]` entry for §3.2.6 states the Note's own second answer — a half-width European numeral mixed with Japanese text is cl-24 — and `A.24/digit-zero/half-width-numeral`'s own case already reads this exact input for that reason, crediting §3.2.4, §3.2.6, §3.9.1 and §3.9.2 but not §3.2.2, whose own sentence is what supplies the fact that a half-width font is one of the two this document itself sanctions for a European numeral in horizontal composition, rather than an arbitrary choice the caller made unprompted. `docs/decisions/european-numeral-by-code-point.md` is the adjacent, narrower reading this case does not need: that decision is about which occurrences count as 'a European numeral' for §C.2 note 11's own trailing-postfixed-abbreviation exception, read from the code point alone rather than from a declared role; this case's own subject is a different sentence entirely; the digit here is simply declared on the half em, the frame §A.24 states for all ten of its digit rows, and §3.2.6's Note is what turns that declaration into cl-24. §A.24 gives U+0030 the Remarks cell 'half-width' (`spec/derived/appendix-a.tsv`'s own row), §A.19's listing of the same key states no width at all, and §A.27's states 'proportionally-spaced', so the half-em frame this occurrence declares is met by §A.24 alone. `A.24/digit-zero/half-width-numeral`'s own input is reused unchanged below, for the reason the case above reuses `A.27/latin-capital-a/proportional-frame`'s: the new fact this case states is which address is credited, not a new reading of the digit.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.24's row for U+0030 (Remarks "half-width"), with §3.2.6's Note and §3.2.2's own sentence naming half-width fonts (§3.9.1, §3.9.2)

forbidden.why: §3.2.4's Note reaches only full-width and fixed-space numerals; this occurrence declares the half em, which §3.2.2's own sentence names as one of horizontal composition's two sanctioned choices for a European numeral and which §3.2.4's Note does not describe.

§A.27 qualifies 0030 'proportionally-spaced', and §3.2.6's Note gives cl-27 the proportional numerals. This occurrence declares the half-em frame, §3.2.2's own other sanctioned choice, not the proportional one.

cases.quote: Note that Western word space (cl-26) is a one third em space, in principle, except at line head, line head of warichu, line end and line end of warichu.
cases.rationale: This case's own contribution is not the classification itself: `A.26/word-space/third-em-frame` already classifies a third-em-declared Western word space (cl-26) among Latin neighbors, and `A.26/word-space/vertical-writing-mode`'s own `quote` field is this identical sentence, read at the identical third-em frame under the vertical direction. Neither case's `rules` field names §3.2.2 (both credit only §3.9.1 and §3.9.2), so the sentence that states the third-em geometry in the first place has already been read, and even quoted, in this suite without ever being credited to its own home address — the same gap the two cases above close for §3.2.6's content. This case closes it here, reading a bare space alone, the geometry this very sentence states for it. §A.26's own table row for U+0020 carries an empty Remarks cell in both renderings (`spec/derived/appendix-a.tsv`'s own row, `cl-26\t0020` with no remark at all), so Appendix A states no width for cl-26's one member and the third em is entirely this sentence's own contribution, read together with §3.9.1's own opening axis: 'Is the character width full-width, half-width, or something else?' — width first among the six ways an occurrence's positioning differs, which is why the declared frame decides the class before anything else is asked. The same code point, U+0020, is also named by §A.24 and by §A.25, and for this key their two Remarks cells are identical character for character: 'quarter em width' in English, 「位取りの空白／字幅は四分角」 in Japanese (`spec/derived/appendix-a.tsv`'s own two rows) — a quarter-em frame and, in the Japanese half alone, the digit-grouping role recorded as `cl-24-remarks-role-stated-only-in-japanese` in `spec/derived/defects.tsv`. An occurrence declared on the third em meets neither qualification: `xtask/src/classes.rs`'s own `REMARKS` table gives that exact cell (`ja: "位取りの空白\n字幅は四分角"`) the mask `FRAME_QUARTER_EM` alone, with no `FRAME_THIRD_EM` bit set, so §A.24's and §A.25's own listings of 0020 do not survive a declared third em at all — they are excluded at the very first step of the narrowing, by their own stated qualification, before any tie-break over which construct an occurrence belongs to is ever reached. What remains standing is §A.26's own unqualified row alone, which is a materially different shape from the quarter-em coordinate `crates/jlreq-class/src/classify.rs`'s own test module already reads (`resolved("\u{0020}", Frame::QuarterEm, Role::Unstated)`), where all three of §A.24, §A.25 and §A.26 survive together because the caller's declared quarter em matches §A.24's and §A.25's own stated qualification, and their own construct-membership classes are then passed over by `docs/decisions/ambiguous-context.md`'s own published tie-break, marked `Standing::Unstated` because the specification itself decides nothing between them. `A.26/word-space/frame-and-role-unstated`'s own case reaches the identical `Standing::Unstated` answer by a third route rather than this one: that case declares no frame and no role at all, so nothing supplied either satisfies or fails either table's own qualification and all three listings stand for want of any declared width, not because a declared quarter em happens to meet one. At the third em, unlike either of those two coordinates, nothing needs to be passed over at all: only one listing — §A.26's own — ever described the occurrence in the first place. `crates/jlreq-class/src/class.rs`'s own `is_construct_membership` is the fact that makes the difference in `Standing` rather than only in candidate count — cl-24 (`InGroupedNumeral`) and cl-25 (`InUnitSymbol`) are two of the nine classes membership in which is a property of a construct rather than of a key, and cl-26 is not one of them, so an answer reached by elimination over an unqualified §A.26 row and two qualification cells that state a different frame is `Standing::Normative`, the specification's own answer, not this project's own tie-break over the specification's silence. This case reads a bare space with no surrounding text and no declared role, and does not declare a writing direction: `A.26/word-space/vertical-writing-mode`'s own case already establishes, over the identical third-em frame, that §3.2.2's amount is scoped to horizontal writing mode by its own heading while cl-26's membership is scoped by neither §A.26's empty Remarks cell nor any direction-conditional rule this workspace's own `docs/direction-sites.toml` names (JLReq conditions exactly three rules on the writing direction — §3.1.3, §3.2.5 and §3.3.5 — and §3.2.2 is not among them), so declaring one here would assert a fact §3.2.2's own text does not state about the class and would needlessly exempt this case from the direction-parity gate that composes a direction-unstated case both ways and requires bit-identical results; leaving it undeclared is the stronger case for exactly the reason that gate exists.

permitted.source: JLReq §A.26's sole row (U+0020), against the Remarks column of §A.24 and §A.25, read for §3.2.2's own third-em sentence (§3.9.1, §3.9.2)

forbidden.why: §A.24 qualifies its listing of 0020 with a quarter-em frame and, in its Japanese half, the digit-grouping role. This occurrence declares the third em, a frame neither renders of that cell states, so the sentence that would put it in cl-24 does not describe it. §3.9.1 asks the width question before any other.

§A.25's own cell for 0020 states the identical quarter-em qualification §A.24's does, and this occurrence's declared third em meets it no better here than there. Answering cl-25 for a word space declared at §3.2.2's own stated geometry treats every Western word space in horizontal composition as a character inside a unit symbol.
